description: The machine-readable form of the evidence bundle that orcinus-verify returns for a change. It is the structured version of the prose bundle in skills/orcinus-verify/SKILL.md. A bundle is only as strong as its revision binding: every check runs on the bundle revision, so a PASS cannot be carried from one revision to another; the fail-first proof records the pre-fix run separately. A bundle whose overall verdict is PASS must have no check with verdict FAIL or INCOMPLETE and no non-empty unverified_items; anything else is INCOMPLETE or FAIL. Validate with skills/orcinus-verify/scripts/validate_evidence.py (standard library only). Every check that ran (verdict PASS or FAIL) must carry its output: an artifact file (with its sha256) or inline text — a PASS with no reviewable output is not evidence. A bundle with no checks at all is valid only as INCOMPLETE, with a stop_reason saying why the verification stopped — except a docs-only/config-only PASS with every gate waived, which may have no checks. Since v6, every check in a PASS bundle must be recorded by record_check.py (recorded_by + capture_sha256, recomputed by the validator from the recorded fields and the artifact files) - a hand-written check cannot be filed as PASS; FAIL/INCOMPLETE bundles may still carry unrecorded checks.

acceptance_criteria.description: The acceptance criteria. If there are none, the verification must stop (INCOMPLETE), not invent them. An empty list means the verdict is INCOMPLETE, never PASS.

command.description: The exact command that ran. For a recorded check this is the canonical rendering of command_argv (shlex.join, or the shell string when shell is true).

cwd.description: The directory the command ran in.

exit_code.description: The real exit code. 0 means the command succeeded; a non-zero code is a FAIL, not a pass.

name.description: What the check is, named after its gate (for example 'test', 'lint', 'build', 'typecheck').

stderr_artifact.description: Where the stderr is saved. Absolute paths, paths escaping the bundle directory, and symlinks are rejected.

stderr_sha256.description: The sha256 hex of the stderr_artifact file. Required when stderr_artifact is present; the validator checks it matches the file.

stderr_text.description: The stderr, inline, when there is no artifact file for it. One of stdout_artifact, stderr_artifact, stdout_text, stderr_text must be present and non-empty for every check that ran (verdict PASS or FAIL). Must contain a non-whitespace character: whitespace-only output is not evidence.

stdout_artifact.description: Where the stdout is saved (a path, relative to the bundle). Absolute paths, paths escaping the bundle directory, and symlinks are rejected.

stdout_sha256.description: The sha256 hex of the stdout_artifact file. Required when stdout_artifact is present; the validator checks it matches the file.

stdout_text.description: The stdout, inline, when there is no artifact file for it. One of stdout_artifact, stderr_artifact, stdout_text, stderr_text must be present and non-empty for every check that ran (verdict PASS or FAIL). Must contain a non-whitespace character: whitespace-only output is not evidence.

tool_version.description: The version of the tool that ran (for example 'pytest 8.4.2').

unverified_items.description: What this check could not establish. Non-empty means the check is INCOMPLETE, not PASS.

verdict.description: The verdict for this check alone.

recorded_by.description: Which recorder produced this check: 'record_check.py/1' for a check run through skills/orcinus-verify/scripts/record_check.py. Required for a check in a PASS bundle.

capture_sha256.description: The binding hash over the canonical record (command argv, shell, cwd, timestamps, exit code, both stream hashes, content digest, revision) - see record_check.py. The validator recomputes it from the stored fields and the artifact files on disk; a mismatch rejects the PASS.

command_argv.description: The command as the argv list record_check.py ran (never a shell string, unless shell is true - then ['sh', '-c', <string>]). The validator requires command to be the canonical rendering of this list.

shell.description: True when the command was a shell string run as ['sh', '-c', command]; false when command_argv was run directly.

content_digest.description: The content digest (scripts/content_digest.py) of the tree the check ran on, recorded by record_check.py at run time.

revision.description: The commit the check ran on (full SHA), recorded by record_check.py at run time. It is the revision the capture is bound to; it may differ from the bundle revision when the bundle is filed for a dirty tree.

dirty_files.description: Uncommitted files, required when working_tree_state is 'dirty', empty otherwise.

fail_first.description: The fail-first proof (orcinus-verify step 3): the new test failed on the pre-fix code and passes after it. Required when the verdict is PASS for a behaviour change (bug-fix, feature, refactor); record the red run here, never as a check. fail_first.test is the pytest nodeid of the test (for example 'tests/test_sum.py::test_sum_two_decimals'); the red and green JUnit XML reports (red_report / green_report) must list that test with status failed and passed respectively — no report means no PASS. Since round 9 the red run binds to its own revision, not the bundle revision: for method 'worktree' the red revision must be the base (an ancestor of the bundle revision — never the bundle revision itself for a committed fix); for 'revert-at-smallest-scope' it binds via red_diff_sha256; test_file_sha256 ties the test file to the green tree.

failed_before.description: True when the test was shown failing on the pre-fix code.

method.description: How the pre-fix run was done: a separate git worktree (preferred), a revert at the smallest possible scope, or not-applicable when the change has no behaviour to test (say why in the note).

note.description: Why the method was chosen, or why fail-first does not apply.

base_revision.description: The base revision the red run ran on (the pre-fix tree): for method 'worktree', the parent of the fix commit when the fix is committed, or HEAD when it is uncommitted (SKILL.md step 3's <base>). Optional; when present the validator requires fail_first.red_check.revision to equal it.

red_diff_sha256.description: For method 'revert-at-smallest-scope': the sha256 of `git diff HEAD` in the reverted tree at red-run time — the diff that reverts the fix at the smallest scope. Required for a PASS with that method; the validator cannot recompute it after the fix is re-applied, so it binds the red run to a diff a reviewer can reproduce by re-applying the revert.

test_file_sha256.description: The sha256 of the test file (fail_first.test, before the '::') as copied into the red worktree, or as it stood for the red run. Required for a PASS with method 'worktree' or 'revert-at-smallest-scope': the validator requires it to match the test file in the green tree, so the red run ran the same test that passes green (in-toto material).

passed_after.description: True when the same test passes after the fix.

red_check.description: The red run itself: the command, its non-zero exit code, and its output (inline text, or an artifact file with its sha256). fail_first.test must appear in this output and in the passing 'test' check's output — a bare test name with no output proves nothing. The output is corroboration only: the structural link is the red_report / green_report JUnit XML. In a PASS bundle the red run must be recorded by record_check.py like any check (recorded_by + capture_sha256, stdout/stderr as artifacts).

command.description: The exact command that ran the test on the pre-fix code.

exit_code.description: The red run's exit code: non-zero, or it is not a red.

stdout_artifact.description: Where the red run's stdout is saved (a path, relative to the bundle).

stdout_sha256.description: The sha256 hex of the stdout_artifact file.

stdout_text.description: The red run's stdout, inline, when there is no artifact file for it.

recorded_by.description: Which recorder produced this check: 'record_check.py/1' for a check run through skills/orcinus-verify/scripts/record_check.py. Required for a check in a PASS bundle.

capture_sha256.description: The binding hash over the canonical record (command argv, shell, cwd, timestamps, exit code, both stream hashes, content digest, revision) - see record_check.py. The validator recomputes it from the stored fields and the artifact files on disk; a mismatch rejects the PASS.

command_argv.description: The command as the argv list record_check.py ran (never a shell string, unless shell is true - then ['sh', '-c', <string>]). The validator requires command to be the canonical rendering of this list.

shell.description: True when the command was a shell string run as ['sh', '-c', command]; false when command_argv was run directly.

cwd.description: The directory the red run ran in.

content_digest.description: The content digest (scripts/content_digest.py) of the tree the check ran on, recorded by record_check.py at run time.

revision.description: The commit the check ran on (full SHA), recorded by record_check.py at run time. It is the revision the capture is bound to; it may differ from the bundle revision when the bundle is filed for a dirty tree.

stderr_artifact.description: Where the red run's stderr is saved (a path, relative to the bundle).

stderr_sha256.description: The sha256 hex of the stderr_artifact file.

red_report.description: A structured test report for this run: a JUnit XML file (pytest --junitxml), recorded as an artifact with its sha256. The report links the run to fail_first.test structurally, by (classname, name) — the stdout text is corroboration only.

artifact.description: Where the JUnit XML report is saved (a path, relative to the bundle).

sha256.description: The sha256 hex of the report file.

format.description: The report format. Only JUnit XML is accepted: its (classname, name) identity is what the fail-first link is checked against.

green_report.description: A structured test report for this run: a JUnit XML file (pytest --junitxml), recorded as an artifact with its sha256. The report links the run to fail_first.test structurally, by (classname, name) — the stdout text is corroboration only.

artifact.description: Where the JUnit XML report is saved (a path, relative to the bundle).

sha256.description: The sha256 hex of the report file.

format.description: The report format. Only JUnit XML is accepted: its (classname, name) identity is what the fail-first link is checked against.

test.description: The test that proves the behaviour, as its pytest nodeid (for example 'tests/test_sum.py::test_sum_two_decimals', or 'tests/test_x.py::TestClass::test_y' for a method). The red_report must list it as failed and the green_report as passed, matched by (classname, name).

files_changed.description: Every file the change touched. A file outside the requested scope is a finding, not a detail.

findings.description: Findings, each with file, line, and evidence. A blocking finding makes the overall verdict FAIL. Findings with category 'security' or 'data-loss' are blocking whatever their severity says.

evidence.description: The behaviour that proves the finding (a command, an output, or a file).

severity.description: Required. A finding without an explicit severity is treated as blocking (fail-closed).

category.description: What kind of finding this is. 'security' and 'data-loss' findings are automatically blocking, whatever their severity says: a security finding cannot label itself non-blocking. A finding claimed non-blocking must declare a category.

implementer_identity.description: Who implemented the change — the implementer, never the verifier. Must differ from reviewer_identity: a verifier cannot verify their own work.

requirement.description: The requirement as the verifier understood it, in their own words.

reviewer_identity.description: Who verified — the verifier, never the implementer. A name, a session id, or an agent id.

revision.description: The exact commit the checks ran on (full or abbreviated SHA), or 'working-tree' with the state in working_tree_state. A PASS is bound to this revision only.

schema_version.description: The schema version. Bump it when a required field is added or a rule changes. v6 requires recorded checks (record_check.py) for a PASS bundle. A PASS with a required test gate additionally needs a JUnit test_report (round 8, FND-005); the field is optional and no previously valid bundle changes version, so the version stays v6.

stop_reason.description: Why the verification stopped before any check ran (for example 'no acceptance criteria were given'). Required when checks is empty and the verdict is INCOMPLETE; a docs-only/config-only PASS with every gate waived may have no checks. A non-empty stop_reason is accepted only on an INCOMPLETE bundle with no checks — any other shape is rejected (round 9, FND-006).

test_report.description: A structured test report for the required 'test' gate: a JUnit XML file (pytest --junitxml), recorded as an artifact with its sha256. Required when the verdict is PASS and 'test' is in required_gates: the report must list at least one test and at least one passed test — a zero-test run ('no tests ran') or an all-skipped suite is not a passing gate. The report is corroboration of the recorded test check, not proof the command ran (a lying command can fabricate a report file too).

artifact.description: Where the JUnit XML report is saved (a path, relative to the bundle).

sha256.description: The sha256 hex of the report file.

format.description: The report format. Only JUnit XML is accepted: its testcase counts are what the test-gate rule checks.

unresolved_risks.description: Risks that remain after the change (for example 'the 3.9 matrix has never run in CI').

unverified_items.description: What could not be checked, and why. Non-empty means the overall verdict cannot be PASS.

verdict.description: The overall verdict. PASS requires every check PASS, no blocking findings, and no unverified items. FAIL means a blocking finding. INCOMPLETE means a check could not run or evidence is missing.

working_tree_state.description: 'clean' (no uncommitted changes) or 'dirty'. If 'dirty', dirty_files must list the uncommitted files, and a PASS must also record diff_sha256.

verification_plan.description: The plan the verification was run against: the change type, the gates this change had to pass, and the gates that do not apply, each with a reason. A bundle whose verdict is PASS needs this plan; every required gate needs a passing check with the same name, and every canonical gate (build, lint, typecheck, test) must be required or explicitly waived. A behaviour change (bug-fix, feature, refactor) additionally needs the test gate and a fail-first proof.

change_type.description: What kind of change was verified. bug-fix, feature and refactor are behaviour changes: a PASS for one needs the test gate and a fail-first proof. docs-only and config-only have no behaviour to test.

not_applicable_gates.description: Gates this change does not need, each with a reason.

required_gates.description: The gates this change had to pass, by the exact check name that proves each one. Every canonical gate (build, lint, typecheck, test) must appear here or in not_applicable_gates with a reason; silence is not a waiver. May be empty for docs-only/config-only when every gate is waived.

diff_sha256.description: The sha256 of `git diff HEAD` for a PASS on a dirty tree: a dirty tree has no revision, so the PASS is bound to this diff instead.

title: ORCINUS verification evidence bundle
